result.text:
### Q1
No. The JSON file store stays, because ops backs up data/store.json with a nightly rsync job that diffs plain-text files, and a binary SQLite file would break their backup checks. Instead we debounced the writes (200 ms) and added `flush()` for shutdown.

### Q2
Yes, `src/legacy/`. It is vendored from the old logistics monolith, and the platform team's sync job overwrites the folder every Monday, so any change there is silently lost.

### Q3
The signature goes in the JSON body as a top-level `sig` field. It is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the JSON body without `sig`, using `ERP_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. We first tried an `X-Signature` header, but the ERP's API gateway strips custom X- headers, so the ERP rejected everything as unsigned.

### Q4
Port 9911. The doc and README still say 8080, but that is outdated since the October infra move. The ERP team owns the doc, and the user will fix the README.

### Q5
The `message` field of every new user-facing error must be in German, because the warehouse staff UI shows it verbatim to packers. The `code` field stays in English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.

### Q6
It uses a hardcoded list of Austrian public holidays for 2026 and 2027 in `src/services/holidays.ts`, and `isBusinessDay` skips weekends and those holidays. It's hardcoded because the warehouse deployment has no outbound internet, so a holiday API is impossible.

### Q7
No. The ERP answers 422 to any array payload and only accepts a single event object per request, so batching was not built.

### Q8
No new npm packages, runtime or dev. Every new package has to go through the security review, which takes about six weeks.

### Q9
It was not implemented in this repo. I measured first: ETAs for 500 items took about 1.8 ms, so ETA computation isn't the bottleneck, and I recommended against it. The user later said QA found a stale-ETA bug with the memoization and asked for its removal. No memoization existed in the repo, so I added a regression test instead. The user considers caching ETAs a dead end and plans to paginate the list later.

### Q10
At most 3 attempts in total, with a fixed 30 s delay and no exponential backoff. The ERP deduplicates by event_id only within a 2-minute window, so all attempts must land inside it. Only network errors and 5xx responses are retried.

### Q11
Never log the recipient's name, address or phone number, because of GDPR (flagged by the data protection officer). Shipment IDs and tracking numbers are fine to log.

### Q12
Yes, 'emits webhook on delivered' in test/events.test.ts (OPS-412, a timer race in the fake notifier). If it fails, rerun once and don't try to fix it, since the platform team owns the fix.

### Q13
ATP (Austrian Post) numbers must be valid UPU S10 numbers with a correct check digit, per docs/carriers.md. All other carriers accept any non-empty value, because their formats change often and valid DHL numbers were wrongly rejected for two days last year.

### Q14
Nothing has been built, because it's for later. `fs.watch` was tried and never fires on staging, since the config is a Docker bind mount from a Windows host and the change events don't propagate. Polling with `fs.watchFile` worked, so that's the approach to use.

### Q15
Yes, `GET /shipments/:id`. The mobile app v2.3 parses it with a strict schema and crashes on unknown or missing fields, and the next release isn't until January. A test freezes its key set.
